LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.2: Rhythm

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Rhythm. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What constitutes rhythm in music?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compose a four- bar rhythmic pattern in 2 4 time
2. write rhythmic patterns in 2 4 on monotone from dictation
3. appreciate rhythmic patterns created by self and others

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RHYTHM
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Rhythm helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: RHYTHM
Study Rhythm like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Compose a four- bar rhythmic pattern in 2 4 time

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a four- bar rhythmic pattern in 2 4 time. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a four- bar rhythmic pattern in 2 4 time.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a four- bar rhythmic pattern in 2 4 time. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write rhythmic patterns in 2 4 on monotone from dictation

What this means
In this part you learn to write rhythmic patterns in 2 4 on monotone from dictation. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write rhythmic patterns in 2 4 on monotone from dictation.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rhythm in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write rhythmic patterns in 2 4 on monotone from dictation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate rhythmic patterns created by self and others

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate rhythmic patterns created by self and others. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate rhythmic patterns created by self and others.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate rhythmic patterns created by self and others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Rhythm is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: compose a four- bar rhythmic pattern in 2 4 time)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rhythm in your own words. (skill: write rhythmic patterns in 2 4 on monotone from dictation)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate rhythmic patterns created by self and others)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Rhythm to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: compose a four- bar rhythmic pattern in 2 4 time.
3. Practise this skill: write rhythmic patterns in 2 4 on monotone from dictation.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate rhythmic patterns created by self and others.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Rhythm from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Rhythm: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Rhythm?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What constitutes rhythm in music?
2. How are rhythmic patterns used in sports?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Rhythm means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: compose a four- bar rhythmic pattern in 2 4 time.
5. Be able to: write rhythmic patterns in 2 4 on monotone from dictation.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
